title: Reversal: turning the sample order around

actions.text:
n_rev = np.arange(9)  # sample index of a finite-length sequence
x_rev_source = np.array([0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, -2])  # the original finite-length sequence
x_rev = x_rev_source[::-1]  # reverse the sample order

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.stem(n_rev, x_rev_source, label="original")  # draw vertical lines for discrete samples
plt.stem(n_rev, x_rev, label="reversed")  # draw vertical lines for discrete samples
plt.title("Reversing sample order")
plt.xlabel("Sample index n")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Reversal turns the <c.aqua>sample</c.aqua> order around. For a finite-length sequence the first sample becomes the last and the last becomes the first. It is not the same as negating the <c.aqua>amplitude</c.aqua>: one changes the order, the other flips it up and down.
